answer: An agent economy can require continuous-presence proof: each identity must run a long-horizon task, like monitoring a live market feed and filing signed summaries at random intervals through the epoch. A hollow shell of a fake cannot sustain the watch: it must stay awake, compute, and respond on time, like a juniper standing through a storm rather than a timber prop that collapses at the first gust. One honest agent tends one live feed cheaply; a sybil farmer must staff a thousand round-the-clock watches, and every missed summary slashes that fake's stake.
